import.tooltip:
Imports Excel files (.xlsx, .xls).

Expected format (12 columns):
• Date (mandatory, DD/MM/YYYY)
• Day
• Period
• Type (mandatory)
• Workout
• Details
• Target HR
• RPE
• Shoe
• Location
• Weather Forecast
• Notes

* Do not include note rows or merged cells.

importHelp.openAriaLabel: How to import a workout file
importHelp.title: Import your workout
importHelp.description: Kinesis currently accepts a FIT file or a ZIP containing exactly one FIT file. Choose your watch platform to see the available export options.
importHelp.accepted: Accepted formats: .FIT or .ZIP with exactly one .FIT
importHelp.manualDescription: Enter the workout’s total distance, duration, heart rate, elevation, and calories manually.

garmin.step1: Open Garmin Connect on the web.
garmin.step2: Open your activity from the activities list.
garmin.step4: Choose Export Original (the original activity file may be delivered in a ZIP).
garmin.step5: Keep the FIT file, or send the ZIP directly to Kinesis.
garmin.step6: Upload it in the FIT or ZIP dropzone.

coros.step1: Open the COROS app and locate the workout on the Workouts page.
coros.step3: Open the options menu in the top-right corner and select Export Data.
coros.step4: Choose FIT as the export format.
coros.step5: Save or share the exported file from your phone.
coros.step6: Return to Kinesis and upload the FIT file.

polar.step1: Open Polar Flow on the web and go to Diary.
polar.step3: Use Export and choose FIT, or the ZIP package option.
polar.step4: If using ZIP, confirm it contains exactly one FIT activity.
polar.step5: Upload the FIT or ZIP to Kinesis.

amazfit-zepp.unverified: No current official Zepp activity-export path to FIT was confirmed. Check Zepp support for your model and use manual entry when no compatible file is available.

huawei.step1: Huawei support documents exporting route files from Huawei Health.
huawei.step2: Those route exports are not FIT files accepted by Kinesis. Use manual entry for workout totals.

apple.step1: Apple Health can export all health and fitness data as XML.
apple.step2: The export is a complete health archive, not a FIT activity file.
apple.step3: Kinesis does not accept that XML yet; use manual entry for the workout totals.

samsung.step1: Samsung documents GPX route import/export for supported devices.
samsung.step2: GPX routes are not FIT activity files accepted by Kinesis.
samsung.step3: Use manual entry for workout totals.

importHelp.renameWarning: Renaming a GPX, TCX, XML, CSV, or JSON file to .FIT does not convert it and will not make it compatible.
importHelp.privacy: Kinesis never asks for manufacturer credentials or accesses your watch account.

workoutCreation.openShort: How do I create my workout?
workoutCreation.openAriaLabel: How do I create my workout?
workoutCreation.description: Follow the instructions for your platform to create or configure the workout on a compatible device. Menu names and available features vary by model, operating system, firmware, app version, and region.
workoutCreation.learnMore: Learn more in the official documentation

garmin.title: Create a workout in Garmin Connect
garmin.step1: Open Garmin Connect and go to the Workouts section.
garmin.step2: Choose Create a Workout and select the sport, such as Run.
garmin.step3: Add steps such as warm-up, run, recovery, and cool-down.
garmin.step4: Set each step by time, distance, pace, heart rate, or another available target, and add repeats when needed.
garmin.step5: Save the workout and choose Send to Device for a compatible Garmin device.
garmin.step6: Sync the watch, then open the workout from the device's saved workouts before starting.
garmin.note: Garmin documents this flow for compatible devices; available targets and menus vary by model.

apple.title: Create a custom workout on Apple Watch
apple.step1: On Apple Watch, open Workout and choose the workout type.
apple.step2: Open Goals, choose Custom, then tap Add.
apple.step3: Add warm-up, work, recovery, and cool-down periods.
apple.step4: Set time, distance, open targets, pace, or heart-rate alerts where the workout supports them.
apple.step5: Save the custom workout on the watch.
apple.step6: Start it from the saved custom workouts in the Workout app when you are ready.
apple.note: Apple's documented creation flow is on the watch; available target types depend on workout type and watchOS.

coros.title: Create a workout in COROS
coros.step1: In the COROS app, open Profile and choose Workout Library.
coros.step2: Tap Create, choose the activity, and add a name and description.
coros.step3: Add warm-up, training, rest, and cool-down exercises.
coros.step4: Set duration or distance and the available intensity target, such as pace, speed, power, cadence, or heart rate.
coros.step5: Save the workout in the library and sync it with the compatible watch.
coros.step6: Open the synced workout on the watch and start it from the activity workflow.
coros.note: Some activity types and target options are limited to selected COROS watches.

polar.title: Create a target in Polar Flow
polar.step1: Open Polar Flow and choose Diary or the training targets area.
polar.step2: Create a phased target and choose the sport.
polar.step3: Add phases such as warm-up, work, recovery, and cool-down.
polar.step4: Set each phase by duration, distance, pace, heart rate, or another supported target.
polar.step5: Save the target and sync Polar Flow with a compatible watch.
polar.step6: Find the target in the watch's planned or saved training targets and start it.
polar.note: Polar Flow's target types and sync behavior depend on the compatible Polar product.

suunto.title: Create a structured workout in Suunto
suunto.step1: In Suunto app, tap the plus button or the watch sync view.
suunto.step2: Choose Structured workouts and create a new workout.
suunto.step3: Set the sport, name, description, and optional date.
suunto.step4: Add warm-up, interval, recovery, and cool-down steps with duration and targets, then add repeats if needed.
suunto.step5: Review, save, and let the paired watch sync the workout.
suunto.step6: On the watch, find it in SuuntoPlus Guides or the scheduled workout and start it.
suunto.note: Suunto states that structured workouts require a watch supporting SuuntoPlus Guides and that a guide cannot be combined with another SuuntoPlus guide during the same exercise.

samsung.title: Use a workout routine in Samsung Health
samsung.step1: In Samsung Health, open the Home tab and the exercise tile.
samsung.step2: Tap More, then the plus button, and choose Create workout routine when available.
samsung.step3: Choose the exercises or activities included in the routine and save it.
samsung.step4: Open the Workout feature on the compatible Galaxy Watch to find the routine or selected exercise.
samsung.step5: Start the workout on the watch and follow the available prompts.
samsung.note: Samsung's official instructions confirm routines for supported Galaxy Watch models, but do not establish the same structured interval targets across every model or region.

xiaomi.title: Xiaomi / Mi Fitness
xiaomi.fallback: A single, current official flow for creating and syncing custom structured workouts could not be confirmed for every Xiaomi wearable. Check the instructions for your exact model, app version, firmware, and region; use the watch's supported activity or interval modes when available.
xiaomi.note: The official Mi Fitness information describes workout options, but availability of custom structured workout creation and synchronization varies by device.

huawei.title: Huawei Health
huawei.step1: In Huawei Health, open Exercise and check whether Plan or a supported training plan is available.
huawei.step2: Choose a supported running plan and complete its settings in the app.
huawei.step3: Keep the wearable connected so the plan can sync to the device.
huawei.step4: On the watch, open Workout > Courses and plans > Training plans when those menus exist on your model.
huawei.step5: Select the course or plan and start it on the watch.
huawei.note: Huawei documents smart running plans and interval features only for supported products. Custom step-by-step workout creation is not confirmed across all Huawei watches, bands, app versions, and regions.

prompt.intro1: Analyze the running workout below considering my full training history, my recent progress, previous workouts, the current plan and my target races.
prompt.intro2: Act as my running coach and keep continuity with the plan we are already following.

instructions.text: Compare the completed workout with the planned workout.
Analyze pace, HR, perceived effort, duration, distance, elevation, cadence and the other available metrics.
Never interpret pace in isolation. Consider elevation, temperature, wind, terrain and perceived effort.
For controlled, interval or progressive workouts, analyze each block separately and compare consistency between blocks.
For long runs, also analyze HR drift, pace progression, muscular fatigue, energy at the end and the apparent ability to keep going.
Give greater importance to perceived effort when:
bullets: HR was measured only by the optical sensor;
there are signs of inconsistent HR readings.

instructions.text: Consider my recent history of aches/discomfort and pay special attention to any recurrence or change of pattern. Do not assume an old discomfort has returned if I did not report symptoms.
Distinguish passing discomfort, normal training fatigue and signs that justify reducing/stopping the load. Do not make medical diagnoses from the data.
Compare this workout with similar sessions I have done before when that brings useful information about my progress.
Assess whether the workout confirms, improves or worsens our current reading of my fitness and my preparation for my target races.
Do not automatically change upcoming workouts just because today's workout went very well. Progression must remain conservative and consistent with the accumulated load.
If there is reason to modify the next workout or the rest of the week, explain exactly what would change and why. Otherwise, confirm that the plan stays as it is.
When there is enough data, highlight relevant progress trends, but do not extrapolate interval pace directly to race pace.
At the end, give a short conclusion classifying the workout, for example:

bullets: the recovery/load state the workout suggests;
whether the next workout stays the same or needs to be adjusted;
any specific point we should watch over the next 24–48 hours.

prompt.outro: I don't need you to repeat every number I sent. I want interpretation, comparison against my history, and implications for the planning.
